quick.summary: What a retention curve shows, and the one point on it that matters most.
quick.takeaway: Watch where the curve flattens. That is who stays.

beats.line: My manager asked if people stick with the new app. How do I show that?
With a retention curve. Start with everyone who joined in one week.
Then plot how many are still active each week after.
It always drops at first. Many people only try things once.
The point to watch is where it flattens out.
Isn’t the big early drop the scary part?
Partly. What decides it is whether it flattens, and how high.
About a quarter of new users stick, from week four on.
Clear, honest, and easy to compare next month.

quiz.question: On a retention curve, which part best shows whether people stick with a product?
options: The total number of sign ups
quiz.explanation: The flat part shows the share of people who keep coming back; a curve that never flattens loses everyone.

quiz.question: A large early drop on a retention curve always means the product is failing.
quiz.explanation: Most products lose many people early. What matters is whether the curve flattens and at what level.
